analysis:
The only change in this PR is test-only: provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift, head lines ~807-839. It adds two tests. `scopedMatchedSequence` exercises `EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence(candidates:generatedText:scope:)` with a GPT-OSS stop-string scope from `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`. It expects a stop string such as '.' to match only in the final channel, not in analysis-channel text. `translationCarriesStopScope` checks that `EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request` propagates `stopStringScope` onto `CBv2Request`, and that the field is nil when no scope is passed. No production code is in the supplied units, so the behavior of the scope logic itself was not reviewed. Only the two base-text units of the test file were supplied; the head-side additions are visible only through the patch excerpt.

Security relevance is limited. This is stop-string and finish-reason handling, which affects output correctness and billing completion counts (T-007 / TB-002 integrity), not confidentiality or authorization. The test code touches none of the cache and tenant-isolation behavior (T-041, cacheSalt) and none of the encryption, attestation or key-handling assets. It adds no new attack surface, no secrets and no network or disk behavior. Existing tests in the file, such as `bridgeStampsCacheSalt`, continue to pin that caller-controlled fields do not become cache identity. Open question for the next pass: the production changes (`ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, `EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence` with `scope`, `CBv2Request.stopStringScope`) are in other batches. Check there that a stop-string scope cannot be used to bypass max-token or usage accounting, and that usage reporting is unchanged.
